author: Alex Hunt
text: I would do Design and Modeling of Biomimetic Humanoid RobotsPut an interesting photo on your first slide for people to look at while settling in

author: Alex Hunt
text: Spend more time making the case for your work. In fact, use the structure of your dissertation almost exactly. Your motivation section is multiple paragraphs long. What are all the good reasons to pursue this work? What are the gaps in knowledge preventing the ideal success? Spend at least 5 minutes/10 slides setting things up.

text: This work fills in four knowledge gaps for the development of more mimetic humanoid robots

author: Alex Hunt
text: Before you show off your model, show some other models and explain how they are insufficient. For example after you explain how they work. You say that because of this complex relationship between force and all these other parameters, a good model is needed in order to design robots. next slide: FESTO has a tool that predicts actuator strength, but it is inaccurate. Then point out all the inaccuracies.next slide: Specific models have been built for specific lengths, but they do not generalizenext slide: I built a test setup to collect a lot of data and fit some models tonext slide: My model captures the behavior that shorter BPAs deliver less maximum isometric forceAll this stuff is published work! Do not shortchange it. Instead, you should lean on it as it is the most fundamentally sound.

text: Slides often need different figures than papers.http://journals.plos.org/ploscompbiol/article?id=10.1371/journal.pcbi.1003833

author: Alex Hunt
text: This equation is confusing. Not enough background. For a presentation, always ask yourself, do I really need this equation? What is it telling my audience?

author: Alex Hunt
text: Set things up better. I would create singular figure that simply captures all the things you have done. It can help transition stuff. So a humanoid with a BPA about a joint. Probably make the joint bent so you can show off Force*distance = joint torque. And a super simple representation of the nervous system. Then, you can zoom in on the BPA for the first section. Then for the second, you zoom out a little and say let's talk about joint torques. Then lay out how muscles create joint torques from the biological sense. Show some opensim stuff. Some opensim joint torques for different muscles. Then say, 'So to make a biomimetic robot, we will want to reproduce these joint torques". next slide: if we hook up the bpas like in a human, we don't get those joint torques.Then there are maybe some options. You could use that to talk about the optimizer. Or you could just jump to and say 'Also, when we built a robot, attached the muscle, and measured the torque, it was wrong. Then spring into the mechanical setup. Probably option B as I think waiting to talk about the optimizer moves a little more nicely into the full design.

author: Alex Hunt
text: It seems that your peer-reviewable work takes up only 15 slides of your 83 slide presentation. That ratio is way off. I've given you lots of ideas on how to expand. You will need to shrink down the rest of this significantly. Extra slides can always go after your thank you slide.Focus on the story. Be a storyteller. The slide titles should tell the story for you.

author: Alex Hunt
text: SADb may or may not fit nicely into your story. I would say it isn't need for a good dissertation presentation and may be a distraction from the main storyline.
